In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cold acclimation is a dynamic, multicomponent and multifaceted process in Rhododrendron leaves, and that the EST data sets generated in this study are useful for identifying genes that are differentially expressed during cold acclimatiion.
the ESTs from the NA and CA leaves of Rhododendrom are a rich source of cDNA clones that can be used to study cold acclimation of evergreen woody plants.

the probability of differentially expressed ESTs picked 1-3x from a library of 430 ESTs (or 1% of the library) is a reasonably accurate predictor for their true differential expression in cold acclimated leaves of Rhododendrom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cold acclimation is associated with the upregulation of genes involved in lipid biosynthesis and desaturase, malate metabolism, cell dehydration avoidance and cell wall biosynthesis in Rhododrendron.
the combination of EST data and Northern blots is a powerful tool for identifying cold acclimation-related genes in woody evergreens.
the ESTs are a powerful resource for the study of gene expression and gene discovery in Rhododondron, especially for genes that are differentially expressed in response to cold acclimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability of upregulation/downregulation of moderately abundant cDNA based on the ESTs can be a reasonable predictor of their'real' upregulation/down-regulation.
the use of moderately abundant cDNA clones can be a powerful tool for gene discovery and functional analysis in plants.
the probability of differentially expressed moderately abundant genes based on EST data is a reasonable predictor of their 'actual' upregulation in cold-acclimated leaves.
